bib.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models

question: Can vision-language pre-training be made compute-efficient by bridging a frozen image encoder and a frozen LLM with a small trainable module?
hypothesis: A Q-Former pre-trained in two stages (representation learning, then generative learning) bridges the modality gap better than an image-to-text generation loss alone.
contributions: Q-Former bridges frozen image encoder and frozen LLM, pre-trained in two stages
SOTA on VQA, captioning, retrieval with fewer trainable parameters
Generic: benefits from stronger unimodal models

method.summary: A 188M-parameter Q-Former with 32 learned queries extracts features from a frozen ViT; stage 1 trains it with ITC, ITG and ITM; stage 2 projects its outputs via one FC layer as soft prompts to a frozen OPT or FlanT5. Pre-trained on 129M images with CapFilt synthetic captions.
method.task: vision-language pre-training; VQA, captioning, image-text retrieval

datasets.name: Pre-training mix (COCO, Visual Genome, CC3M, CC12M, SBU, LAION400M subset)
datasets.preprocessing: CapFilt: 10 captions from BLIP-large per image, ranked with the web caption by CLIP ViT-L/14 similarity, keep top 2, sample 1 per step; 224x224, random resized crop + horizontal flip

datasets.name: COCO
datasets.split: Karpathy test for captioning; 5K test for retrieval

datasets.name: VQAv2 (+ Visual Genome train samples)
datasets.split: fine-tune on train+val of VQAv2; eval test-dev/test-std; zero-shot eval on val and test-dev

models.name: Q-Former
models.architecture: two transformer submodules sharing self-attention; cross-attention every other block; 32 queries x 768 dim

other.note: last layer removed, second-last layer features used
last layer removed, second-last layer features used

training.objective: Stage 1: ITC (in-batch negatives, max over queries) + ITG (multimodal causal mask, [DEC] token) + ITM (bidirectional mask, hard negatives, mean of per-query 2-class logits). Stage 2: LM loss (OPT) or prefix LM loss (FlanT5) through one FC layer; frozen ViT and LLM.
training.precision: FP16 frozen ViT and LLM; BFloat16 for FlanT5

other.finetune_captioning(Table 7): 5 epochs, warmup 1000, lr 1e-5, bs 256, AdamW (0.9,0.999), wd 0.05, drop path 0, res 364, prompt 'a photo of', beam 5, ViT layer-wise LR decay 1 (FlanT5XL, OPT2.7B) / 0.95 (OPT6.7B)
other.finetune_VQA(Table 8): 5 epochs, warmup 1000, lr 1e-5, bs 128, AdamW (0.9,0.999), wd 0.05, drop path 0, res 490, prompt 'Question: {} Answer:', beam 5, LLRD 0.95/0.95/0.9 for FlanT5XL/OPT2.7B/OPT6.7B
other.finetune_retrieval(Table 9): 5 epochs, warmup 1000, lr 5e-6 (ViT-L) / 1e-5 (ViT-g), bs 224, AdamW (0.9,0.98) ViT-L / (0.9,0.999) ViT-g, wd 0.05, res 364, LLRD 1 / 0.95
other.finetune_scope: LLM frozen; Q-Former and image encoder updated in captioning and VQA; retrieval fine-tunes ViT+Q-Former without LLM

inference.prompting: Zero-shot VQA: OPT 'Question: {} Answer:'; FlanT5 'Question: {} Short answer:'; instructed generation appends text prompt after visual prompt
inference.retrieval: k=128 candidates by image-text feature similarity, reranked by ITM

eval.protocol: single reported runs; no seeds or significance tests stated

results.claim: BLIP-2 ViT-g FlanT5-XXL beats Flamingo80B on zero-shot VQAv2 test-dev by 8.7 points with 54x fewer trainable parameters.
results.setup: Zero-shot, ViT-g + FlanT5XXL (12.1B total params); beam 5, length-penalty -1, prompt 'Question: {} Short answer:'; Flamingo80B has 10.2B trainable
results.table: Table 2, row BLIP-2 ViT-g FlanT5XXL, column test-dev
results.quote: It outperforms Flamingo80B by 8.7% on VQAv2, despite having 54x fewer trainable parameters.
results.note: 8.7 is the absolute gap 65.0-56.3 (points). Table 2 lists 108M trainable for this model, Table 1 lists 188M for BLIP-2; 54x matches 10.2B/188M. Val score 65.2.

results.claim: Without the first-stage representation learning, zero-shot VQA is substantially lower and OPT suffers catastrophic forgetting; exact numbers only in Fig 5.
results.setup: ViT-g with OPT6.7B and FlanT5-XL, zero-shot VQAv2 over 80k iterations
results.quote: In particular, OPT suffers from catastrophic forgetting where performance drastically degrades as training proceeds.

results.claim: Using a single 16-A100(40G) machine, the largest model needs under 6 days for stage 1 and under 3 days for stage 2.
results.quote: our largest model with ViT-g and FlanT5-XXL requires less than 6 days for the first stage and less than 3 days for the second stage.

results.claim: BLIP-2 shows no VQA improvement from in-context examples, attributed to pretraining on single image-text pairs per sample.
results.quote: our experiments with BLIP-2 do not observe an improved VQA performance when providing the LLM with in-context VQA examples.

results.claim: Stronger image encoder or stronger LLM both improve zero-shot VQA (ViT-g>ViT-L; larger LLM > smaller; FlanT5 > OPT).
results.quote: a stronger image encoder or a stronger LLM both lead to better performance.

limits: No gain from in-context examples (single image-text pair per sample pretraining)
Outputs can be wrong: inaccurate knowledge, wrong reasoning path, outdated info (Fig 6)
Inherits LLM risks: offensive language, social bias, privacy leakage
Zero-shot gains reported on single runs without seeds
Trainable-parameter counts differ between Table 1 (188M), Table 2 (103-108M) and fine-tuning tables (1.1-1.2B) without explanation
